candidates.rationale: A gap that opens beyond the prior session's own high-low range reflects an overnight shock that liquidity providers in liquid large caps typically fade, so the gap's size relative to the prior day's range should predict a partial reversion toward that range.

A stock accelerating toward the top of its own 21-day closing range is more likely showing a durable re-rating than noise when the firm also screens high on operating margin, so the interaction should out-predict either leg alone.

A sudden widening of today's high-low range relative to its own trailing-quarter history marks a shift into a higher-realised-volatility regime, and in large caps such regime shifts tend to mark the start of a fresh short-horizon directional move rather than pure noise.

Ranking near a 12-month high while having pulled back only over the last week isolates intermediate-term momentum from the well-documented one-week reversal that contaminates raw short returns, and scaling by realised volatility puts the signal on a comparable risk footing across names.

A stock whose recent high occurred more recently than its recent low has current directional pressure tilted upward, and that tilt is more likely to persist into a real trend when the firm is also operationally efficient (high asset turnover).

A rising ratio of downside to upside realised volatility captures building negative return skew (down days growing disproportionately larger than up days), an early distribution-risk signature that tends to continue rather than mean-revert in large caps.

An accelerating rise in a stock's own relative trading-activity ranking shows participation building ahead of or alongside a price move, distinguishing information-driven demand (which needs volume behind it) from noise-driven price changes.

The open aggregates overnight order flow separately from the intraday auction that sets the close, so a stock opening near the top of both its 10-day and 63-day range reflects durable, multi-horizon-consistent overnight demand, a channel distinct from close-based momentum.

A larger average intraday pullback below the open than rally above it signals weak intraday buying support, and that asymmetric selling pressure is a more worrying, more persistent signal for firms already carrying more financial leverage.

A stock simultaneously near a 10-day high in both trading activity and daily range is having a genuine, participation-backed volatility event rather than an idiosyncratic single-day fluke, which for liquid large caps should mark a new information regime that persists over subsequent sessions.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Re-normalizing a volume field inside a denominator already keyed on that field doesn't decorrelate: CS_RANK($dollar_volume) vs raw $dollar_volume in the same guarded ratio hit rho 0.981, and TS_MEAN/TS_SUM smoothing both legs of an existing RANK(fundamental)*RANK(dollar_volume)-style product hit rho 0.910-0.915. Vary the field or window family, not the wrapper.
  2. For $book_per_share, a 63-day point change (TS_DELTA) is weak alone even normalized by close (cheap_screen |t| 0.84); the same window's dispersion (TS_STD) crossed with accrual_gap accepted at 2.963. Favor dispersion over point-change for this field.
  3. A guarded denominator built from TS_STD($volume, 21) collides with the existing volume-z-score archive block regardless of the numerator (archive_subtree, 5 shared nodes). Use a different window or a $dollar_volume-based dispersion in that slot instead.
  4. Swapping which aggregate (MEAN vs MIN/MAX) fills the same slot in a $close/$low/$high range-position formula doesn't decorrelate (rho 0.984) — vary which fields occupy the slots, not which TS_ aggregate summarizes one of them.
  5. Don't propose RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(X) for any X: this exact template drove 4 of 6 correlation rejects this round (X = volume, dollar_volume, or a short price/volume ratio-delta), all rho 0.92-1.00 against existing archive members regardless of which X was tried.
  6. Drop $return, raw price deltas, and EMA-crossover-of-close (MACD-style) as a standalone or dominant leg: 9 of 20 rejects this round failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.15-0.93) this way, including wrapped in COUNT, TS_DECAY_LINEAR, TS_ARGMAX, or crossed with TS_RANK(volume) -- smoothing or longer windows don't rescue it.
  7. Don't subtract a raw TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, w) leg against a fundamental TS_DELTA via CS_ZSCORE: the volume-delta leg is independently dead and drags the pair below the cheap-screen bar (0.54) even when the fundamental side uses a compliant 63-day window.
  8. Before submitting a ($close-$low)/(stat) or ($close-$high)/(stat) style ratio wrapped in TS_MEAN or crossed via CS_RANK, check whether the denominator/other-field fragment already exists in the archive: 3 of 20 rejects this round were archive_subtree hits from swapping just one OHLC field or denominator field while a >=5-node fragment rode along untouched.
  9. Dedupe each round's proposal batch against itself before submitting: 2 of 20 rejects this round (10%) were exact within-run duplicates, a pure wasted evaluation slot.
  10. $close and $adj_close are the same series for correlation purposes (rho 1.000 this round); don't resubmit a formula with one swapped for the other expecting a different score.
  11. A raw $volume <-> $dollar_volume swap inside an otherwise-identical ratio/TS_MEAN shape still collapses (rho 0.963 this round); stop using that swap alone as a decorrelation technique.
  12. The strongest accepts this round crossed a two-fundamental product ($operating_margin * $accrual_gap) against a $dollar_volume magnitude or delta term (fitness 2.3-3.9, niches slow/mixed/low and slow/fundamental/low); this fundamental-product-times-volume-magnitude family is validated and worth extending to other fundamental pairs.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
